messages:
emma: Quick Q — if we need to immediately toggle off the realtime-v2 rollout in prod, who formally takes custody of the toggle and what minimal evidence do we need for post-action audit? planning to run a fast canary rollback if latency spikes :eyes:

raj: Oncall lead (that's usually you) can flip in an emergency. Required: 1) state in this thread why (one short sentence), 2) paste the toggle command you ran, 3) screenshot or paste of the toggle service response, and 4) notify #incidents + product + owner.

sarah: Adding detail: SRE policy says flips by non-oncall need a 2-person approval. So if a dev wants to hit it, oncall must ACK and an SRE lead or EM must consent. We don't grant blanket rights during business hours without that.

lee: For realtime-v2 the safest quick command is the toggle API (no console):
```
curl -X POST https://toggles.internal.redwood/api/v1/toggle -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOGGLE_KEY" -d '{"key":"realtime-v2","state":"off","reason":"latency-spike:95p-ms>1500"}'
```
That returns a JSON with audit id. Save that id in this thread.

emma: Thanks — two practical followups: 1) if we flip, how long can a dev 'borrow' custody to run a patch? 2) who shards the rollback across regions so we don't create partial state?

raj: Borrowing custody: max 30 minutes by default. Extend only with explicit ack from SRE lead + note here with duration. For region sharding, the toggle supports scope param `regions:[us-west-*, eu-*]`. If you flip global, you must confirm with infra team first.

sarah: Escalation flow: oncall flips -> page owner -> if no ack in 10m, page EM -> if still no response, escalate to SRE director. Always tag incident with `incident:<thread_ts>` (use the thread_ts above). Post-action: attach the audit id, screenshots, and a short summary (what we observed and why we flipped).

ops-bot: toggle-service recorded action: toggle=realtime-v2 state=off actor=emma audit_id=aud_3020013388 timestamp=3020013388

lee: Also add: run the quick sanity smoke after flip: `./tools/smoke-check --env=prod --path=/health --concurrency=5` and paste 3 sample latencies here. If latency is back to baseline, keep canary off and start rollback test plan.

emma: Perfect. I'll document this as a brief checklist for next oncall rotation. For immediate case: I'll flip if 95p > 1500ms and paste the audit info here. tagging @raj @sarah @lee :thumbsup:

raj: One more nit: we keep a deletion TTL for temporary flips in the toggle DB. If you flip for emergency, set `expires_in=30m` in the payload so it auto-reverts unless extended. Prevents forgotten kills.

sarah: And capture a small log snippet from the proxy showing error rates (1m window) and attach. That is gold for postmortem triage.

lee: Noted. I'll prepare the small snippet script and put it in the runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/realtime-v2-toggle (adding there now).

emma: OK flipping if latency crosses threshold. Will paste results here.
